Teaching support: Two algorithms can test properties in different orders yet classify every input consistently. A complete classifier uses explicit definitions, covers every input, and survives tests with boundary cases.
Worked example: A test set already covers Square, Non-square rectangle, Non-square rhombus. Type the group still needed to test all four outputs. Answer: Other quadrilateral. Every intended output needs a valid test example.
Reasoning example: Which test set gives evidence that a four-way quadrilateral classifier covers squares, non-square rectangles, non-square rhombuses and other quadrilaterals? Answer: One valid example from each of the four groups, including a square.. Each intended output needs a test, including the overlap case.
Application example: A test set already covers Square, Non-square rectangle, Non-square rhombus. Type the group still needed to test all four outputs. Answer: Other quadrilateral. Every intended output needs a valid test example.
